Why Maize Homes Need Pest Control

Maize sits squarely in USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 6b, where winter temperatures drop to negative five degrees but rarely stay there long. The 78 freeze days per year and 36 freeze-thaw cycles create a challenging pest pattern: insects and rodents don't die off completely in winter, they simply move indoors. When temperatures fluctuate between our average high of 69°F and low of 49°F, pests remain active longer than residents expect.

The city's location in the Corn Belt means agricultural pests naturally migrate toward residential areas, especially during harvest season and after the 33 inches of annual rainfall saturate fields. Homes near Delano Township and along the edges of town experience particularly heavy pressure from field mice, grain beetles, and occasional cricket invasions. The Cowskin Creek, currently running at a gauge height of 11.13 feet, adds moisture to the local environment that attracts mosquitoes, spiders, and moisture-loving insects throughout the growing season.

With a median household income of $77,371, Maize families have invested significantly in their properties. Protecting that investment means addressing pest problems before termites compromise structural integrity or rodents damage insulation and wiring. Kansas has faced 100 federal disaster declarations in the past decade—99 of them severe storms—and post-storm conditions create ideal breeding grounds for pests in damaged structures and standing water.

The National Weather Service monitors our area through their ICT office using KICT radar, and they've documented how our nine inches of annual snowfall melts into conditions that drive pests indoors during the freeze season from October through April.

Our Pest Control Process In Maize

Shaw's Pest Control starts every service with a thorough inspection of your property's interior and exterior. We examine foundation cracks, entry points around utility penetrations, moisture issues in crawl spaces and basements, and conducive conditions in attics and garages. Our Master Tech Certified technicians identify not just the pests you're seeing, but the underlying conditions that attracted them in the first place.

We apply targeted treatments using EPA-approved products selected specifically for the pests common in Sedgwick County. Our exterior barrier treatment creates a protective zone around your home's perimeter, while interior spot treatments address active infestations in kitchens, bathrooms, and other problem areas. We pay special attention to the moisture-prone areas that come with Maize's climate, treating crawl spaces and foundations where spiders and crickets congregate.

Every treatment comes with a detailed explanation of what we're doing and why—no pressure, no upselling, just honest recommendations based on what your home actually needs. Our Three State Certifications mean we're qualified to handle pest issues across Kansas and beyond, but we've chosen to focus on serving our local community where we've built relationships since 1987.

Follow-up visits ensure treatments remain effective through seasonal changes. We adjust our approach based on whether we're preparing your home for the freeze season, addressing spring emergence, or protecting against summer activity when Maize's good air quality and comfortable temperatures bring everyone—including pests—outdoors.
